source: low graphics long storyline mobile-related Mech game at the start you are ejected from a warship down onto a planet landing in a forest the forest is named ayush also you land with your team you have three other teammates AI you can give them commands follow assist retreat stay here or go over there and you point to a location you want them to go one of your teammates has long range weapons another one of your teammates has short range weapons and the last teammate you have has heavy weapons you have medium range normal weapons that you can upgrade by finding resources over the forest your mission is to figured out what happened to the last team that came down there are side quests you can do to get upgrades and credits in game currency the map is extremely large you can fast travel between locations but you have to unlock it by doing a main quest near the start you unlock a dropship that takes you from location to another location across the map and if fast forwards till you reach there making you go between locations quickly your enemies are red and black aliens that have plasma weapons that want to kill you and stop you

answers.ask: Roughly how many distinct locations should the map hold, and is the forest the whole world or one region of it?
answers.answer: Make Ayush Forest the whole playable world, with about 6 distinct locations spread across it; this keeps the first build manageable while supporting the long storyline and dropship travel.

answers.ask: Is there a safe base or settlement anywhere, or is the whole map hostile forest?
answers.answer: Include one small safe landing-zone base near the start for the team and dropship; the rest of Ayush Forest is hostile alien territory.

scene_prompt: Create a low-graphics 3D mech combat map set across Ayush Forest, an extremely large forested planet that forms the whole playable world. The team begins after ejecting from a warship, landing at a small safe landing-zone base near the forest edge, with space for the squad and a dropship pad. About six distinct locations are spread widely through the hostile forest and connected by long ground routes, including a main early-story location near the starting base; the dropship travels between unlocked landing areas. Dense woodland, uneven natural terrain, and scattered resource sites fill the spaces between locations, while red-and-black alien forces occupy hostile areas.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is `RPG`, with `Action` as a secondary combat layer. Character upgrades, resource gathering, quests, hostile alien combat, and a safe resupply point make progression RPG the owner of the world shape.

### Shape and preset
Use `world-open`: Ayush Forest is one contiguous playable world, not separate dungeon instances, with six widely spaced locations connected across the same forest. The closest preset is none: the world supports open exploration and combat, but it does not establish the biome-distance progression or player-base loop of Open World & Survival RPG.

### Config requirements
Use `safezone-town` as a compact fortified landing-zone base near the forest edge, with squad staging space and a clear dropship pad. Use `hazard-aggro` for hostile alien-held clearings set away from the main travel routes. Use `collectible-nodes` as visible resource-site alcoves scattered through woodland and terrain. Use `teleporter-link` as standardized unlocked dropship landing pads at major locations.

### Layout requirements
Place `spawner-npc` origins within each hostile location, behind alien-held cover or at the far side of combat clearings, so red-and-black plasma-weapon aliens enter from readable directions. Place one `teleporter-link` endpoint at the safe base and one at each of the five other locations; these are dropship arrival pads unlocked through progression. Place `collectible-nodes` in small clusters beside long routes and within hostile areas, rather than in the base.

### Layout components
The six locations are: the small safe landing-zone base at the forest edge; one early-story site close to it; and four further hostile locations distributed broadly across Ayush Forest. The base contains a squad arrival area, dropship pad, and protected open ground. Long dirt and worn-metal ground routes radiate from the base and branch through dense woodland toward each destination. Keep the early-story location on the nearest route; place the other four at increasingly remote points without making them separate maps. Terrain is uneven forest floor with shallow rises, gullies, rocks, and dense tree clusters. Scatter resource sites between locations and in alien-held clearings. The world boundary is concealed by impassable dense forest and natural terrain. Compose the map as a broad readable forest expanse, with the base visibly distinct and hostile sites separated by substantial travel distance.

### Render order
Use `topdown` first and make it authoritative, because the large connected forest needs reliable route connectivity between all six locations; it is not a maze or racing circuit, so it does not use procedural carving.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Scale is huge, driven by the explicitly extremely large forest world and widely separated six locations. Theme: low-graphics, low-poly sci-fi mech warfare in a dark alien forest. Pipeline modifier: `P0`; the map is one contiguous ground surface with no required overhangs, interior transitions, separate maps, or topology that must be generated by construction.
